body: Natalia Katona is a freelance commodity analyst, based in the United Arab Emirates. Situated off California’s Santa Barbara coast, the Santa Ynez project operated by Sable Offshore has become a litmus test of President Trump’s determination to revive oil production in a state pursuing a future beyond it. After a decade of shutdowns, its return depended on the Trump administration’s intervention in a prolonged regulatory battle. Originally developed by ExxonMobil, the Santa Ynez complex comprises the Hondo, Harmony and Heritage platforms and their associated onshore infrastructure. Its troubles began in May 2015, when Plains All American’s Line 901 pipeline ruptured due to external corrosion near Refugio State Beach, spilling almost 3,000 barrels of crude . The failure cut off the project’s route to local refineries and broader market, forcing production to stop. ExxonMobil eventually sold the assets to Sable in 2024 for a total consideration of $643 million . Restarting the production proved difficult. Pipeline safety requirements, permitting disputes and court orders kept the development from returning to normal operations. Those obstacles unfolded against Democrat-led California’s broader push to reduce its dependence on fossil fuels: in 2021, Governor Gavin Newsom asked state regulators to analyze how to phase out oil extraction by 2045 . Sable announced in May 2025 that it had restarted production from Harmony, a claim California officials disputed , saying the activity was well testing. The offshore platforms sit in federal waters, beyond the state’s direct reach, but the oil initially went into storage while its onshore pipeline route, which California regulated at the time, remained blocked. The Trump administration then helped reopen that route in two steps. In December 2025, the federal Pipeline and Hazardous Materials Safety Administration (PHMSA) reclassified the onshore pipelines as interstate infrastructure at Sable’s request, asserting federal oversight, and approved their restart plan on Dec. 22 . After the conflict between the US and Iran started in late February 2026, just as the ensuing energy crisis hit the markets, Energy Secretary Chris Wright invoked the Defense Production Act to direct the restoration of operations on March 13 , citing supply risks and military dependence on foreign oil. Sable resumed pipeline shipments the following day. However, California’s Democratic administration challenged both interventions, turning the project’s revival into a continuing fight over federal and state authority. Democratic control of the House and Senate, won in the early November midterms , will not automatically reverse those decisions. The new Congress takes office in January, while Trump retains executive authority and the ability to veto legislation. But congressional committees can investigate the administration’s intervention, demand records and use spending negotiations to seek restrictions. Members of California’s congressional delegation have already started: in May they wrote to Sable’s CEO asking the company to preserve records and promising continued oversight in the next Congress. For Sable, the likely exposure is greater scrutiny and less scope for additional legislative support, rather than an immediate congressional shutdown. Courts remain the more direct threat to the legal foundations of its pipeline operations. On Tuesday, the BLS reported Core CPI at 0.3% , above the expected 0.2%, and CPI m/m at 0.4%, higher than the expected 0.3% for the month of October. This continues to be a thorn in the side of doves, and should continue to put pressure on the Fed to remain restrictive. Fridayâs labor report gave the market an additional policy input that shouldnât be ignored. The Bureau of Labor Statistics reported that nonfarm payroll employment increased by 165,000 jobs in October, while the unemployment rate came in at 4.1%. The labor market is still expanding, which can reduce pressure for rapid monetary easing, although payrolls alone donât determine Federal Reserve policy. Nonetheless, more employment typically means that more consumers are out there, with inflation having that input. For gold, the overall relevant information runs through expected policy rates, nominal Treasury yields, inflation compensation, and the dollar, rather than just through employment itself. A higher inflation reading supports goldâs store-of-wealth narrative, but it could also lift yields if investors expect a firmer policy path. A softer reading could reduce nominal and real yields while also weakening demand for inflation protection. The shape of the real yield curve also deserves attention. On November 6, the 30-year real yield was 3.07%, above the 20-year rate of 2.91% and the 10-year rate of 2.63%. This upward slope implies investors demand progressively more inflation-adjusted return at longer maturities. For the gold market, the long end can matter through portfolio allocation and the cost of carrying defensive positions. A fall confined to short maturities would be less supportive than a broad decline across the entire curve. Strong productivity can allow output and wages to grow with less inflationary pressure, potentially modifying and moderating the monetary premium embedded in gold. title: Gold Price Recovers Above US$4,000 As Analysts Forecast Further Gains - DirectorsTalk Interviews
body: Gold prices recovered on 11 November after falling sharply in the previous session, with the precious metal holding above the US$4,000 per ounce level despite renewed concerns over inflation and the prospect of higher US interest rates. Spot gold traded around US$4,040 per ounce, following a decline of approximately 3% on Tuesday. Stronger-than-expected US inflation data and expectations of further Federal Reserve tightening had contributed to the earlier selling pressure. The latest recovery comes as analysts assess whether the recent correction represents a temporary setback or a change in the broader direction of the gold market. The US$4,000 level has emerged as an important support area, with prices managing to remain above it despite pressure from higher bond yields and a stronger US dollar. Standard Chartered maintains a positive outlook, forecasting an average gold price of US$4,650 per ounce during the fourth quarter of 2026, followed by a further increase to US$4,850 in the first quarter of 2027. The bank points to continued investment demand and central bank purchases as important sources of support. Gold-backed exchange-traded products attracted 211 tonnes of investment demand during the third quarter, their strongest quarterly inflows since 2024. A further 19 tonnes entered these products during October. Central bank purchases also remained significant, reaching 321 tonnes in the third quarter, above Standard Chartered’s estimate of 200 tonnes. Continued official-sector buying has provided an additional source of demand as central banks diversify their reserves. The bank also considers gold’s ability to maintain support above US$4,000 despite stronger economic data an indication of underlying market resilience. However, a move above US$4,200 would represent the next significant technical level to watch. CPM Group has also maintained a constructive view of the precious metals market following the recent correction. The research group considers the latest decline a period of consolidation following several days of gains, rather than evidence that the broader upward trend has ended. Its assessment points to continued demand for precious metals amid concerns surrounding economic uncertainty, government debt, inflation and geopolitical developments. Uncertainty over technology company valuations and wider financial market conditions has also contributed to interest in alternative stores of value. body: Advanced Micro Devices Inc. shares jumped 9.5% on Wednesday. Strong results from AI cloud provider CoreWeave and an upbeat analyst report on server processors drove a broad rally in semiconductor stocks. AMD stock traded at $564.17 in afternoon trading, up 9.50%. It outpaced Nvidia, which gained about 5%. The move added to a sharp rebound from last week's AI selloff. The rally began after CoreWeave reported third-quarter results late Tuesday that beat analyst forecasts. The company reported revenue of $3.66 billion and raised its full-year 2026 revenue forecast to between $13.0 billion and $13.3 billion, according to The Motley Fool. CoreWeave also said it plans capital investment of $37 billion to $39 billion. Analysts said that points to continued heavy spending on data center chips, including AMD's processors. CoreWeave shares surged more than 25%. AMD also got a boost from a UBS report on server processor sales. UBS analyst Timothy Arcuri said server CPU shipments rose 31% from a year earlier in the third quarter. He said AMD's server CPU market share held steady at about 28.4%, while Intel's share fell 2.4 percentage points. Arcuri also believes CPU prices are rising, which could boost AMD's profit margins. He projected that CPU sales could reach $210 billion by 2030. At AMD's current market share, that would mean nearly $60 billion in CPU sales for the company. AI systems increasingly need powerful central processors alongside graphics chips, which has fueled demand for AMD's EPYC server processors. Goldman Sachs analyst James Schneider said AI stocks were "clearly in oversold territory" and named AMD, Nvidia and Broadcom as top picks. He described AMD as "very attractive" for growth, though less compelling on valuation. AMD has a 12-month median price target of $650, based on 56 analysts, according to The Motley Fool. AMD reported record third-quarter revenue of $13.4 billion earlier this month, up 45% from a year earlier and above analyst expectations. Adjusted earnings per share came in at $2.09, up 74% and ahead of forecasts. Management said demand exceeds supply. The company increased inventory by about $3 billion in the quarter to $11.5 billion to meet strong data center demand. Free cash flow fell to $554 million in the quarter from $1.9 billion a year earlier, which management attributed to working capital and spending on capacity. AMD pairs its Instinct AI graphics chips with EPYC server processors in its Helios rack-scale systems. Jensen and Lori Huang's Nvidia fortune is jointly controlled. How that makes things complicated now that he's resigned
summary: Jensen Huang’s $140 billion stake in Nvidia is largely held by trusts co-owned with his wife, Lori, creating added uncertainty for his financial future.
body: Jensen Huang's $140 billion stake in Nvidia is largely held by trusts that are co-owned with his wife, Lori, creating added uncertainty for the shares and his financial future following his resignation from the company, according to attorneys and SEC filings. Huang and his wife jointly own about 800 million Nvidia shares worth roughly $135 billion through a complex web of trusts and LLCs created for tax and estate planning purposes, according to SEC filings. Jensen Huang directly owns about 70 million shares valued at about $12 billion. While owning company stock through a trust is common among tech founders and CEOs, it's less typical for a founder to have equal ownership with a spouse, tax experts say. The arrangement further complicates Huang's sudden exit from the company, but could prove to be a stabilizing force for the shares, since the trusts make it more difficult for either Huang or his wife to quickly sell. "Each of Mr. Huang and his wife may be deemed to have shared beneficial ownership of, and to exercise shared voting and investment power over," according to an SEC filing. According to the filings, Jensen and Lori Huang own about 530 million shares as co-trustees of the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Living Trust, created in 1995. They're also co-trustees of the Huang 2012 Irrevocable Trust, which owns 31.4 million shares, and the Huang Irrevocable Remainder Trust, which owns 109 million shares. About 135 million shares are held by LLCs that have the Living Trust as the sole member, according to the filings. Lori Huang is the president of the Jen-Hsun and Lori Huang Foundation, which owns 69 million shares and reported $9 billion in net assets in 2024, according to IRS filings. Each of the trust structures serves different tax or estate purposes, according to trust and estate attorneys. The living trust is likely a revocable marital trust, since it was created 10 years after the Huangs married and two years after Nvidia was founded in 1993. Attorneys say living trusts help couples avoid the potentially expensive and public probate process when one spouse dies. Many couples, for example, create living trusts for homes they purchase or other assets. The main tax benefit of living trusts is that when one spouse dies, the surviving spouse gets a step-up in basis for the entire trust's assets, rather than just their half, according to attorneys. While the rules of each living trust vary, attorneys say shares in the living trust can typically be sold or divided fairly easily in the case of a divorce. "It's like a joint checking account," said Kathleen Martone, partner at Varnum LLP. While the revocable trust would typically allow each of them to sell their shares, lawyers said it is common for executives or their trusts to have agreements with the company limiting the sale or transfer of shares to prevent large-scale liquidation. "In the event they divide shares in their revocable trust, there's probably transfer restrictions. He may have to hold them for her benefit, and she would get the monetary benefit of the shares but not voting or management rights," said Leslie Evans, partner at Withers. "He could retain the stock while Lori receives other assets or an equalization payment." The more complicated structures used by the Huangs, and the ones with the largest tax benefits, are the irrevocable trusts. The SEC filings state that "Mr Huang and his wife are co-trustees" of both trusts. With an irrevocable trust, the creator transfers ownership of an asset into the trust and the terms can't be changed without the consent of the beneficiaries or a court. Attorneys say the 2012 irrevocable trust is likely an "intentionally defective grantor trust," a type of irrevocable trust where the creator gifts assets but is still treated by the IRS as the owner of the property for income tax purposes. The structure allows the creator to lend money to the trust to buy the shares, as well as pay income taxes for the trust when it earns money

title: India October CPI inflation rises to 6.09%, food inflation accelerates to 8.94%
summary: India CPI Y/Y 6.09% vs 5.93% expected Prior 5.54% Full report India's CPI rose to 6.09% y/y in October, according to provisional data, pointing to increased price pressures in the economy. The headline inflation rate was higher in rural areas, where prices increased by 6.63% y/y, compared with 5.41% in urban areas. Food inflation was a big standout, with the Consumer Food Price Index rising 8.94% y/y in October. Food price increases were relatively broad-based across the country, with rural food inflation reaching 9.09% and urban food inflation standing at 8.68%. The figures highlight the significant contribution of food prices to India's inflationary pressures, with food inflation running well above the headline CPI rate. Overall, the October report points to a challenging inflation environment for the Reserve Bank of India. Given the acceleration in inflation, the market is pricing in a 69% chance of a 25 bps hike at the next RBI meeting, with 31% probabilitiy of a larger 50 bps move. The US-Iran war has been a major contributor of inflation through higher crude oil prices, increasing India's import bill and raising transportation, energy and agricultural production costs. As a major oil importer, India is particularly vulnerable to prolonged disruptions in the Middle East. Higher energy and fertiliser costs gradually feed into consumer prices, while a weaker rupee also makes imports more expensive. This article was written by Giuseppe Dellamotta at investinglive.com.

body: The UK economy looks to have pulled off a surprisingly resilient end to the third quarter, with growth conditions picking up in September. The beat on estimates comes as the services sector outperformed, albeit also with a negative revision to the August figures. Overall, this sees the UK economy grow by 0.7% on the quarter - matching estimates in the preliminary report here . Looking at the details, there were positives all around with the services sector growth being the standout. But at the same time, industrial and manufacturing output also posted growth in September in defying negative expectations. So, that also helped to underpin the stronger economic mood in wrapping up Q3 2026. The more detailed breakdown shows that 9 of the 14 subsectors grew in the services sector, with the largest positive contribution coming from real estate activities (+0.4%). The second largest positive contribution to services sector output in September came from transportation and storage (+1.4%). Overall, this report will do little to distract the BOE outlook as policymakers continue to keep their eyes focused on the inflation battle. With growth conditions still holding up, there will be lesser headwinds for the BOE in wanting to justify another bank rate increase in December before reassessing their policy path again come next year. GBP/USD is keeping at around 1.3260 on the day, down 0.1% on the day and not too much changed from the data release with traders having priced in roughly 71% odds of a 25 bps rate hike for next month coming into today. body: UK Vows Global Climate Leadership as PM Doubles Down on Net Zero What I Cover Tsvetana Paraskova is an energy and commodities journalist who has contributed to Oilprice.com for nearly a decade, covering global energy markets, commodities,… The booming AI industry is consuming more and more power with each data center springing up across the United States. The surge in power demand necessitates grid upgrades and expansions in the energy infrastructure. But the costs are not allocated fairly, and households end up picking up the bill. Among residents, the costs are also disproportionately distributed, with the heaviest burden falling on rural and lower-income households, Cornell University researchers say. This week, Cornell researchers published a study in the scientific journal Nature Energy, which analyzed growth in energy demand and infrastructure projects for four major U.S. power grids from 2020 to 2025. The research found that data centers hiked wholesale electricity prices last year. But these same data centers paid just 38% of the infrastructure costs linked to their growth, or $3.12 billion out of an $8.25 billion bill in 2025. The remaining 62%, or a massive $5.13 billion bill, fell largely on residents, “with the lowest income households seeing extra energy costs up to 28% of their incomes,” Cornell researchers said . Transmission investment in energy infrastructure projects surged from $2 billion in 2020 to $34 billion in 2025, with data centers driving much of that rise, the research has found. In regulated tariffs, residential users are allocated a median of 47% of costs despite contributing far less to demand growth, leading to disproportionate energy burdens. The cost sharing forces rural communities to bear increases 76% larger than urban communities, the researchers wrote in the study. The core of the problem with household bills and the growing backlash against data centers, which became clearly evident in the midterm elections, lies in the way the costs for new power projects are currently being allocated. At present, the allocation is often based on previous patterns of energy consumption, not on forecasts of future growth. “It’s kind of a chicken-and-egg problem,” said Fengqi You from the Cornell Duffield College of Engineering and co-author of the study. “Because if you’re going to build a data center, you need to expand this power infrastructure. Otherwise, there’s no electricity for them to run. But before they build, they’re not using energy,” You added. “So with this model of relying on past consumption, households end up taking on much of the infrastructure costs.” Moreover, the study found that the current cost-sharing rules mean that residents in New Jersey, Pennsylvania, and Ohio help pay for grid upgrades linked to data center growth in Virginia. “You do not have to live next to a data center to help pay for its power infrastructure,” You said. “The grid connects communities across states, and cost-sharing rules connect them financially.” You and the study’s first author and Cornell postdoctoral researcher Cheng Feng recommend changes to cost-sharing rules to lower the burdens on communities, as well as various state-level measures to charge data centers directly in line with the new demand they add. States could also set up programs, such as a recent law in Minnesota that created a special revenue fund in the state treasury to which money must be transferred from the fee on qualified large-scale data centers. The fee revenue must be used only for utility programs benefiting low-income households, per Minnesota’s new law. The backlash against data centers in the midterms, and residents’ concerns that communities are paying and will keep paying for the infrastructure upgrades needed to power these data centers, are stirring debates in many states and in Congress, which the Democrats will control from 2027. body: UK Vows Global Climate Leadership as PM Doubles Down on Net Zero Angola has accelerated efforts to diversify its economy away from heavy dependence on oil by using this year’s windfall oil revenues to fund reforms and investments in transport corridors, minerals, banking, and tourism industries, according to Citigroup. “We’re definitely seeing a lot of activity and it has the benefit of longer-term political stability, economic stability, which is making it more attractive for foreign direct investment, infrastructure projects, and other longer-term investment,” Citi’s Grant Carson, who oversees several African markets including Angola, told Bloomberg in an interview published on Thursday. Angola’s government is working to diversify the economy away from the extraction-led model of the past decades, the Citi executive told Bloomberg on the sidelines of the African Financial Industry Summit in Angola’s capital city of Luanda. The African country, which relies on crude oil for about 90% of its export revenues, has seen in recent months deals in the banking, tourism, and agriculture sectors as the diversification drive is gaining momentum, Carson said. Angola is also relying on expanded transport links, such as the U.S.-backed Lobito Corridor , a railway network to link the minerals-producing regions in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and Zambia with Angola’s Port of Lobito on the Atlantic Ocean. Angola’s state oil firm, Sonangol, is also seeking stakes and footprints in the development of critical minerals domestically. Yet, Angola remains vulnerable to global oil prices, Fitch Ratings said last week as it affirmed its Long-Term Issuer Default Ratings (IDRs) on the country at 'B- ‌ ' with a Stable Outlook. Angola’s oil production is set to remain broadly stable at around 1 million barrels per day (bpd) over the next year, while new and incremental projects should subsequently offset natural decline and support stabilization of production, the ratings agency said. “But with oil accounting for close to 60% of fiscal revenues and 95% of exports, fiscal and external financing conditions remain highly exposed to oil sector developments and prices,” Fitch noted. body: UK Vows Global Climate Leadership as PM Doubles Down on Net Zero What I Cover Tsvetana Paraskova is an energy and commodities journalist who has contributed to Oilprice.com for nearly a decade, covering global energy markets, commodities,… Nigeria’s crude oil output averaged 1.51 million barrels per day (bpd) in October as OPEC’s biggest African producer pumped to its quota for the sixth consecutive month, data from the Nigerian Upstream Petroleum Regulatory Commission (NUPRC) showed this week. Nigeria last month pumped a total of 1.688 million barrels of crude oil and condensate per day, according to the data from its upstream regulator. Excluding condensate production, which is not part of the OPEC+ production quotas, Nigeria’s crude oil production alone averaged 1.51 million bpd, or 101% of the 1.5 million bpd ceiling set by the OPEC+ deals. Nigeria’s stable crude oil output in recent months was due to enhanced operational stability, improved production uptime, and efficient crude flows, the NUPRC said. Nigeria’s crude oil output jumped to a 15-month high in May, when production averaged 1.53 million bpd, the highest level since January 2025, as the African country started producing oil at its ceiling per the OPEC+ group’s agreements, after years of failing to do so due to sabotage, oil theft, and oil spills. In the early weeks of the Iran war, Nigeria was actively increasing its crude oil production in response to major global supply disruptions caused by the closure of the Strait of Hormuz, with authorities aiming to raise output by 100,000 barrels bpd in the immediate term to capture widening supply gaps. Nigeria has struggled to pump to its OPEC+ quota in recent years as sabotage often led to force majeure at major export streams. However, with a recent crackdown on oil theft and sabotage in the Niger Delta, Nigeria has managed to increase crude production and aims for further growth by 2030. Nigeria aims to increase national crude oil production to 2 million bpd by 2027, according to NNPC executive vice president Udy Ntia. body: UK Vows Global Climate Leadership as PM Doubles Down on Net Zero What I Cover Tsvetana Paraskova is an energy and commodities journalist who has contributed to Oilprice.com for nearly a decade, covering global energy markets, commodities,… India has imported higher volumes of crude oil from the Persian Gulf than from Russia so far in November, for the first time since the Iran war broke out and disrupted the normal supply chain through the Strait of Hormuz. So far this month, India is estimated to have imported about 2.1 million barrels per day (bpd) of crude oil from the Persian Gulf, compared to 1.8 million bpd flows from Russia, Bloomberg reported on Thursday, citing data by Kpler. This is yet another sign that Strait of Hormuz flows have materially recovered in recent weeks, thanks to ship-to-ship (STS) transfers that have moved closer to India’s coastlines amid congestion in the Gulf of Oman and fears of attacks on tankers close to the Strait of Hormuz. Before the Iran war, India’s total crude oil imports via Hormuz averaged about 2.8 million bpd. In the early months of the now nine-month-long war, flows from the Persian Gulf to India crumbled to as low as 247,000 bpd in April, when the Strait was closed to almost any traffic. Russia remains a key crude oil supplier to India, but the rebound in Hormuz flows and the shorter distance to India have boosted Indian imports of crude oil from the Gulf producers. Last month, the waters outside the Strait of Hormuz were so overcrowded with ship-to-ship transfers to keep oil flowing out of the Gulf that the STS operations started to expand into India’s West Coast . The Gulf of Kutch, which opens towards the Arabian Sea facing the Gulf of Oman, has become another point of STS for the Gulf oil producers. The Middle Eastern oil exporters look to keep their supplies to Asian markets flowing, despite increased risks to tanker journeys in the Strait of Hormuz. At the end of October, Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL), one of the biggest Indian state-owned refiners, said it would reduce its purchases of crude oil from Russia in November as high freight costs and premiums for Russia’s crude undermine the attractiveness of Moscow’s oil compared to multiple offers for Middle Eastern crude, whose prices are falling. SK Energy, for its part, provisionally chartered a Suezmax tanker to transport crude from Gabon to the South Korean port of Ulsan in December. As a result, freight rates for very large crude carriers have sunk by 50% from October highs, and Suezmax and Aframax rates have also dropped sharply. “The recent freight correction has been driven by improving vessel availability following October’s exceptional market tightness,” Vortexa shipping analyst Wanying Zhang said, as quoted by Reuters. “The number of laden mainstream VLCCs and Suezmaxes in East Asia has increased by approximately 15% since early September, suggesting a growing pool of vessels that could become available as they complete discharge operations.” Tanker rates soared this year due to Middle Eastern producers taking to ship-to-ship transfers outside the Strait of Hormuz. For this, they use shuttle tankers, including smaller carriers, to sneak the oil through Hormuz and then load it on supertankers in the Gulf of Oman. As a result, supertanker rates from the Gulf to Asia hit $1.4 million daily in October before retreating. title: Nvidia turmoil tests metals demand boom
summary: Jensen Huang's exit from Nvidia raises concerns about AI leadership, risking miners reliant on new data centers for metals demand.
body: Jensen Huang’s departure from Nvidia has put the leadership behind the artificial intelligence boom under scrutiny, exposing a risk for miners counting on new data centres and power projects to lift metals demand. Huang resigned Thursday as Nvidia’s (Nasdaq: NVDA) CEO, president and director, with chief financial officer Colette Kress taking over on an interim basis. His departure followed reports of affairs that raised questions about corporate governance and US national security. “This kind of situation would be damaging at any company but is exacerbated by just how strong the key person risk is perceived to be at Nvidia,” Russ Mould, investment director at UK-based AJ Bell with £126 billion ($167 billion) under administration, said by email before the resignation. “Huang is the man who led the business to become the poster child of the [artificial intelligence] story and for a time the largest company on earth.” For miners, the exposure lies in the construction and financing behind that growth. A prolonged loss of confidence could delay buildings, electrical connections and power generation, pushing metal purchases into later years. The scale of any demand loss would depend on which projects are postponed or cancelled. Nvidia shares fell as low as $148 (C$210) Thursday morning, about 30% below the $210 level seen last week, before recovering to trade 7.7% weaker on the day. BMO Capital Markets cut its Nvidia share-price target by 29% to $240 from $340 and removed the company as its top pick in a note issued late Wednesday. It maintained its outperform rating. “We remain bullish on [artificial intelligence]; however, the latest scandal is an overhang,” BMO semiconductor analyst Harsh Kumar wrote. Kumar said a leadership transition could remove distractions, but wanted clarity on a successor before reassessing his position. His note preceded both Huang’s departure and Kress’s appointment. BMO projected Nvidia revenue of $410.9 billion in the fiscal year ending January 2027 and $698.9 billion the following year, an increase of 70%. Those forecasts concern chip and related technology sales, not metal purchases, but show that a sharply lower share-price target can coexist with expectations for substantial business growth. The scale of existing spending helps explain why an immediate collapse in physical demand is far from certain. Microsoft (Nasdaq: MSFT) invested $45.2 billion, including finance leases, in the quarter ended Sept. 30. It expects calendar-year spending of about $170 billion and more than $50 billion in the December quarter, chief financial officer Amy Hood said on its Oct. 28 call . Alphabet (Nasdaq: GOOGL) maintained its $195-billion to $205-billion spending forecast for 2026 and expects a significant increase in 2027, chief financial officer Anat Ashkenazi said on its earnings call the same day. Those forecasts predate Huang’s departure and could still be revised. For miners, the composition of those budgets matters. About three-quarters of Microsoft’s quarterly spending went to shorter-lived assets, mainly processors, including higher memory and storage costs. Alphabet put about 65% of its technical infrastructure investment into servers and networking equipment and the rest into data centres, the companies said. A dollar cut from a chip order cannot be translated directly into a proportional loss of copper demand. Moving workloads to another chip supplier could preserve much of the infrastructure requirement, although equipment designs and metal use would differ. The relevant changes would be fewer buildings, smaller electrical connections or delayed power projects. Copper has one of the clearest connections to the building boom because it carries electricity through power systems and data centres. But AI is only one part of the demand growth on which the mining industry is betting. title: Endeavour bets $1.2 billion on major Ivory Coast gold mine
summary: Construction advances on a major West African deposit targeting 320,000 oz. annually as development costs climb 13%.
body: West Africa-focused Endeavour Mining (LON, TSX: EDV) has approved construction of its $1.2-billion Assafou gold project in Côte d’Ivoire, targeting first production in the first half of 2029 as the company advances one of its largest growth investments. The project is expected to produce an average of 320,000 oz. of gold annually at all-in sustaining costs (AISC) of $1,026 per oz. during its first eight years, according to a definitive feasibility study released in April. Assafou has an initial mine life of 16 years and will use a processing plant designed to handle 5 million tonnes of ore annually. “We will continue to prioritize shareholder returns while we organically grow the business, and we have made significant progress in de-risking our organic growth strategy,” CEO Ian Cockerill said in a release Thursday. The investment decision marks a major step for Endeavour’s expansion plans in West Africa. Assafou, discovered less than seven years before its scheduled first gold pour, is expected to help lift the company’s annual production to 1.5 million oz. by 2030, alongside an underground expansion at its Sabodala-Massawa mine in Senegal. Development budget, however, has risen by $139 million, or 13%, from the $1.06 billion estimated in the feasibility study. The revised figure reflects higher compensation payments, infrastructure costs and additional measures intended to reduce construction and commissioning risks. Increased land and crop compensation accounts for approximately 60% of the budget increase following consultations with local authorities and communities. Power infrastructure revisions account for another 10%, while additional operational preparations and contingency allowances each contribute about 15%. Some costs remain subject to negotiation, including grid connections and the final route of a national highway diversion. Endeavour has awarded the engineering, procurement and construction management contract to Lycopodium, which supported the project’s earlier technical studies. Contracts for major processing equipment are also being finalized, while the company has reached an agreement in principle on the terms of its mining convention with Côte d’Ivoire. Construction preparations are advancing on several fronts. Resettlement work is scheduled to begin in late November, with process plant earthworks expected before year-end. Concrete work is planned for the second quarter of 2027, followed by plant construction and commissioning in early 2029. Work on power infrastructure, tailings and water storage facilities is expected to begin in early 2027. Mining pre-stripping is scheduled for 2028, although Endeavour has yet to decide whether to use contractors or operate its own mining fleet. The company has committed $58.7 million, representing about 5% of the revised capital budget. It expects spending to accelerate in the fourth quarter as compensation payments and deposits for long-lead equipment come due. Endeavour is also investigating more than 20 exploration targets within 10 km of Assafou. Its 2026-2030 exploration program aims to identify another 1 million to 1.5 million oz. of resources across the broader Tanda-Iguela property, potentially extending the operation’s life and improving production flexibility. The investment decision accompanied Endeavour’s third-quarter financial results, which showed record free cash flow of $1.02 billion for the first nine months of 2026, up 50% from a year earlier. body: Phil Mackintosh, Nasdaq chief economist and senior vice president, painted a picture of a resilient economy during the annual MSO Symposium held Nov. 2 and shared his predictions for the year ahead, including lower interest rates. Mackintosh said the markets have “powered through” three big challenges over the last year: tariffs, the war in Iran, and interest rate changes. There are no recessions in the world, and “growth might be slow, but it’s positive enough to weather the shocks like we’ve been seeing,” he said. “We’re definitely seeing the economy sort of turn around; things get more positive or less negative depending on which side of the economy you’re on,” Mackintosh said. “And because of that, in the labor market, we are starting to see a little bit of strength. [At] the start of the year, this was meant to be a really good tailwind for the stock market and a really good tailwind for company profits. It turns out the tailwind is still happening. Hiring is starting to pick back up.” According to Mackintosh, tariffs didn’t create a big dent in the global economy, and have somewhat stabilized. “Initially there was that huge spike in the average tariff rate. It’s actually been coming down,” he said. “They didn’t affect the economy as much as you think, even though for a lot of companies they definitely created a lot of uncertainty,” he said. “In terms of your industry, whether tariffs have impacted inflation much… the answer is not much at all.” “The general trend in this industry in inflation is you’re on a deflationary trend, and now you’ve become deflationary, so the impact of tariffs from this industry onto the CPI [Consumer Price Index] actually is pretty small,” he said. Effects on the oil market from the Iran War were digested much better than might’ve been expected, according to Mackintosh. He said that despite 20 million barrels a day missing from global supply, and the biggest shock to oil supply caused by wars dating back to the 1950s, the price of oil didn’t go up that much. And that doesn’t seem to be getting better when looking at shipping data, he noted. “The war is still active from an economic and supply perspective,” Mackintosh said. As for interest rates, he said they have gone from definitely falling to definitely rising, if you trust the market, and the reason for that is inflation. Mackintosh said interest rates are now hiking quickly because the Federal Reserve waited so long for transitory oil-driven inflation to go away. “The Fed is not sitting there going, ‘Well, oil prices could easily come down to $70 or $60 if we resolve the war and the supply chain fixes,'” he said. “Instead, the Fed is trying to slow the economy down just in case.” And long-term borrowing is starting to cost consumers and companies money, he said. Several developed countries, in addition to the U.S., have seen long-term interest rates increase. “If interest rates and debt both go up, they both add to the amount of costs that we’re all going to have to pay out of our tax receipts or tax bills, so you can see net interest costs becomes bigger and bigger as a problem,” Mackintosh said. He noted that households are trying to stretch how long they’ll own a car, increasing the number of months on a new car loan. “It’s going up and up and up as people try to buy a car that’s going to last longer than the usual cycle,” he said. Mackintosh called himself a contrarian for his prediction that interest rates will be lower in 12 months. title: Nvidia’s Jensen Huang Resigns As CEO With CFO Colette Kress To Step In: Analyst Compares To Apple’s ‘Steve Jobs Moment’ - TradingView
body: Nvidia (NVDA) announced on Thursday that Jensen Huang has resigned as chief executive, president and member of the board, effective immediately. The company said chief financial officer (CFO) Colette Kress would step in as interim chief executive officer (CEO), while continuing in her previous role, until a permanent successor is named. Nvidia added that its board plans to consider internal and external candidates for the post. “NVIDIA’s strength has always come from its people, and together with our leadership team, I am committed to building on the extraordinary foundation Jensen created over the last 33 years,” said Kress. “We will continue advancing the work that has made NVIDIA a leader in accelerated computing and AI, and execute on the opportunities ahead. Our focus remains on serving our customers, partners, developers and shareholders.” Harvey C. Jones, a former CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys, was named the board’s first-ever chair. NVDA stock was down as much as 13% in morning trade, hitting an over-one-year low and on track to log its biggest single-day drop since January 2025, when it fell over 16%. Its market capitalization fell below Microsoft's (MSFT) valuation. Huang’s exit comes after The New York Times reported on Wednesday that he had a second extramarital relationship with an executive, and The Wall Street Journal reported that the board was preparing to oust him. On CNBC, Wolfe Research’s Chris Caso said Huang’s exit was not a surprise. “This is not how you want it to end. But as you said, it’s not a surprise this morning at this point,” he said. “You know it’s sort of like the Apple Steve Jobs moment,” Caso added. “There’s going to be somebody new that’s not Jensen, but you know, it’s not necessarily over.” He said the industry is short of supply, and he pointed to Nvidia’s backlog as a cushion. “Nvidia sold out through the end of next year. The roadmap is set,” Caso stated. He said the key question is who replaces Huang, and that Kress is a good interim choice. CNBC’s Jim Cramer said the exit “had to happen.” He said Kress knows the business and has long been the company’s public voice. “I think she’s going to be terrific at trying to figure out where the pieces are,” Cramer said. “She’ll provide some needed order.” The company said Kress will retain her role as executive vice president and CFO while serving as interim CEO. She joined Nvidia in September 2013. Before that, Kress spent nearly 25 years in finance roles at technology companies, including Cisco (CSCO) and Microsoft (MSFT). Nvidia said she has led the finance team and played a key role in the company’s growth. The board named Harvey C. Jones its first-ever chair. Jones has been an entrepreneur, technology executive and venture investor for more than 30 years. He was previously CEO and executive chairman of Synopsys. “Colette has helped lead NVIDIA through a period of extraordinary growth and has a deep understanding of our business, customers, operations and financial position,” Jones said. He added that the board has “full confidence” in her and the leadership team. “We expect the company’s operations, customer commitments and product roadmap to continue without interruption,” Jones stated. Nvidia confirmed that it will still report its fiscal third-quarter 2027 results on Tuesday next week, after market close. Wall Street is expecting the company to report earnings of $2.47 per share on revenue of $109 billion. Huang's exit hit other chip and AI stocks in morning trade. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing (TSM) dropped over 5% and Alibaba (BABA) fell almost 6% on concerns over export controls. iShares Semiconductor ETF (SOXX) was down nearly 3%. Advanced Micro Devices (AMD) and Broadcom (AVGO) bucked the broader trend and rose, as investors bet that Nvidia’s turmoil could push more business to its rivals.
